newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos, court stop showing of film on Filipina maid.
newsitem.headline: Ramos, court stop showing of film on Filipina maid.

text.p: The Philippines on Tuesday stopped the showing of a film about a Filipina maid who escaped execution in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) after the Gulf state said its screening would harm ties, officials said.

President Fidel Ramos, visiting Bahrain, ordered state censors to defer the film's scheduled public screening on Wednesday "due to anticipated extremely negative impact on Philippines-UAE relations", the presidential palace said.
Showing the film "Sarah Balabagan Story" would also endanger negotiations to save the life of another Filipino jailed in the UAE for killing an Indian national, Ramos said.
Simultaneously, a Manila court issued a temporary restraining order preventing the film's showing after a local Moslem group protested that some scenes were offensive to Islam.
The movie is based on the story of the teenaged Balabagan who was sentenced to death by a UAE court for stabbing to death her Arab employer she had accused of trying to rape her in 1994.
After UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan intervened, the sentence on Balabagan was reduced to one year in jail and 100 lashes.

Balabagan received a heroine's welcome in Manila when she returned last year and has become a symbol of the four million Filipinos working overseas. They include tens of thousands of housemaids and nightclub dancers.
Ramos's order was addressed to the Movie and Television Review and Classification Board which last week blocked the film's premiere by refusing to release a permit for its showing.
The Foreign Office said the UAE had expressed deep concern about the film.
A Foreign Office statement cited the role played by the UAE president in saving Balabagan's life.

It added: "The UAE is now asking the Philippine government to do a similar favour from the President (Ramos), to exert influence to stop the showing of the film which they believe will cause them embarrassment."
The showing of the movie could prejudice the welfare of about 80,000 Filipinos working in the UAE, including several facing criminal charges in UAE courts, it added.
One of them, John Aquino, was originally sentenced to death by a UAE trial court but the Emirates' supreme court in December overturned the ruling and said it would retry the case.
